method: SIGKILL the cmd/orfscrashtest writer mid-append, then reopen read-write (quarantining the abandoned tail) and verify the committed prefix is unchanged
note: real SIGKILL of the cmd/orfscrashtest writer at a random point mid-append, 1000 iterations. The court waits for the writer's first committed transaction (a READY line) and then sleeps a random interval before SIGKILLing, so the crash lands inside an in-progress append. The volume is created with a segment size (genesis frame + one 256-record transaction = 42338 bytes) chosen so every committed transaction ends exactly at a segment boundary, so each append begins in a fresh trailing segment whose id is the recovered committed root; a kill mid-append therefore leaves the abandoned tail in a movable (quarantinable) segment. 342 kills left a tail (2 torn, 340 uncommitted), 342 were quarantined (MOVED, never truncated), and 658 recovered with no tail (the kill landed after a transaction's bytes were complete, e.g. during its fsync barrier). This models a process kill, not power loss: bytes in the page cache survive. Truncations, prefix mismatches and recovery failures are all zero; every recovered volume passed verify --deep and accepted one further committed transaction at the recovered root.
